create.title: Two-saddle endpoint-uniform Fresnel normal form
create.statement_tex: For the accepted beta single-transition phase, collecting the exact linear terms and differentiating the signed Stirling branch gives partial_alpha Psi=log(|alpha|D_j/(pi q sqrt(Xx))). Hence there are two stationary points alpha=plus or minus lambda, lambda=pi q sqrt(Xx)/D_j, with Hessians plus or minus lambda^(-1). For fixed beta,nu the finite alpha interval is [max(beta+nu-U,-2S-beta), min(beta+nu+U,2S-beta)]. On any component with |alpha| comparable to lambda, if the complete signed recombined amplitude has a scale-normalized C^2 norm M, the exact Morse coordinate zeta(y)=sgn(y-1)sqrt(2(y log y-y+1)) gives an incomplete-Fresnel leading term and O(M) remainder uniformly through saddle entry and exit. An exact endpoint saddle has half the full Fresnel coefficient. This lemma is conditional on the scaled C^2 amplitude hypothesis and supplies no outside-height or full-sum estimate.
create.next_action: Prove the scaled C^2 hypothesis only after the finite v-vertical and oriented outside-v sides are recombined in the symmetric top limit.

create.title: Finite-height moving Hilbert-pole logarithmic edge
create.statement_tex: Let C_(a,V)(L)=int_(-V)^V H_b(nu)/(a+i(L-nu))dnu, where H_b is the actual fixed-b beta height amplitude after all nonsingular factors are retained. If H_b is C^1 near V and H_b(V) is nonzero, then C_(a,V)(V)=-i H_b(V)log(1/a)+O_(H,V)(1) as a tends to zero; the analogous formula holds at -V. The accepted height transform is analytic and nonzero on b>0, so admissible actual-profile edge points exist. Therefore an isolated finite-v segment cannot be replaced uniformly by the whole-line PV/delta convolution when the moving pole L=alpha-beta reaches its edge. This does not obstruct the complete finite operator: the logarithm may cancel against oriented outside-v sides or under a justified uniform height-before-top exhaustion.
create.next_action: Derive the exact finite outside-v side in the same coordinates and test cancellation of the logarithmic edge before taking the symmetric top limit.

create.title: Outside-v-side reconciliation of the moving top-pole edge
create.statement_tex: For the connector-completed beta branch at finite U,V,S and positive outside abscissae, combine the truncated v-vertical integral with both oriented outside-v sides, the v=0 height residue, the u=0 top residue and joint corner when crossed, and the exact omega-recombined radial factor. Prove that the symmetric physical top limit exists uniformly as L=alpha-beta crosses plus or minus V, with the logarithmic edge terms cancelled or target-bounded, and then justify a nested U,V,S exhaustion with constants polynomial in b^(-1). The resulting complete signed amplitude must satisfy the scale-normalized C^2 hypotheses of the two-saddle Fresnel lemma.
create.next_action: Write the exact oriented outside-v side and its endpoint expansion in the L=alpha-beta coordinate; compare its log coefficient with the truncated vertical edge before estimating anything.

update.statement_tex: For R1=-(pi i sqrt(X)/rho)I1(rho), let lambda=pi q sqrt(Xx)/D_j. On either signed stationary patch alpha=plus or minus lambda, with bounded beta, fixed b=Re(v)>0, and positive separation from alpha endpoints, finite nu endpoints, rho=0, and v=0, the explicit 1/rho gives q^(-1) relative to unsplit G. After the symmetric full-line hard-top split (a+i mu)^(-1)=pi delta_0(mu)-iPV(1/mu), the signed two-denominator convolution gives a further inverse frequency, yielding local capacity O_b(D_j/(q lambda))=O_b(D_j/(q^2 theta_j(x))). This excludes finite-height edge crossing, transitions without scaled derivative control, artificial-pole and axial seams, the double-bounded share, full sums, endpoints, and outside-height limits.

reject.reason: Differentiating the exact signed Stirling phase gives partial_alpha Psi=log(|alpha|D_j/(pi q sqrt(Xx))), so alpha=-pi q sqrt(Xx)/D_j is a second stationary point.
A pointwise separated saddle bound does not supply the scale-normalized alpha derivatives required by the uniform Morse lemma, especially near the moving hard-top and artificial-rho seams.
When L=alpha-beta reaches plus or minus V, the actual truncated convolution has a nonzero logarithmic edge coefficient unless its oriented outside contribution is recombined.
The q^(-2) local factor omits material h, real-abscissa, profile, radial, transition, endpoint, and finite-side powers; it cannot alone certify the dyadic sum.
